item.title: Salsa Thursdays at Time Out Market — Thu Nov 12, 7:00 PM — Time Out Market New York
item.description:
Join us for one of NYC’s best free salsa nights and turn your Thursday into a dance-floor celebration.
Get your salsa on every Thursday night at Time Out Market New York! Head up to the fifth floor for an electrifying evening of rhythm, movement, and Latin vibes. Whether you’re a total beginner or a seasoned dancer, this is your weekly excuse to move, sweat, and smile. Starting at 7:30 PM, renowned instructor Marlene Veras will guide you through the steps, breaking down the fundamentals so you feel confident on the dance floor. The night is powered by infectious beats from DJ Ray Suave, with live percussion by Jessica La Timbalera, setting the stage for a high-energy salsa experience. After the lesson, the floor opens up for a full-on salsa dance party until 10 PM. Bring a partner or come solo—everyone’s welcome.

item.title: [In]Security: Military Portraiture of Gertrude Kearns — Tue Nov 17, 12:30 PM — Joan Goldfarb Study Centre
item.description:
[In] Security, evokes the tensions between protection and vulnerability, certainty and instability. Made between 2002 and 2026, these works are portraits of real people: Canadian Armed Forces senior officers at critical moments in Canada’s military history. They are also records of the systems around them. Uniforms, maps, borders, slogans, insignia and military jargon move the image beyond likeness, locating the individual within larger structures of geography, conflict and institutional power.
Source: York University

item.description: Students get up close and personal with an eclectic group of authors while earning course credit through LA&PS’ Canadian Writers in Person (AP/CLTR 1953 6.0A) course. They explore the contemporary work of renowned authors, while having the unique opportunity to engage with them in a dialogue about their work. Readings are free and open to members of the public and to members of the York community not enrolled in the course. Our lineups consist of a unique selection of emerging and established Canadian writers, whose writing explores a broad range of topics, and a variety of geographical and cultural landscapes. item.title: [In]Security: Military Portraiture of Gertrude Kearns — Wed Nov 25, 12:30 PM — Joan Goldfarb Study Centre
item.description:
[In] Security, evokes the tensions between protection and vulnerability, certainty and instability. Made between 2002 and 2026, these works are portraits of real people: Canadian Armed Forces senior officers at critical moments in Canada’s military history. They are also records of the systems around them. Uniforms, maps, borders, slogans, insignia and military jargon move the image beyond likeness, locating the individual within larger structures of geography, conflict and institutional power.
Source: York University

item.title: Author Talk: Steven Biggs — Sat Nov 28, 11:30 AM — Toronto Botanical Garden
item.description:
Grow Figs Where You Think You Can’t: Stories, Ingenuity, and Homegrown Figs What makes someone build a “figatorium,” collect hundreds of varieties, or tuck fig trees into bed for a Canadian winter?
Join Toronto horticulturist and author Steven Biggs for a mix of storytelling and practical fig-growing advice celebrating the revised and expanded edition of Grow Figs Where You Think You Can’t.
Meet some of the fascinating growers featured in the book—from a generous mentor in an Ontario backyard to a California fig hunter—and discover the family traditions, curiosity, and ingenuity behind their gardens. Along the way, Steven shares ideas for growing figs here in the Toronto area, getting ripe fruit, and finding room for a little Mediterranean flavour at home.
Whether you already grow figs or are simply curious, come for the stories, bring your questions, and stay for the book signing.
